_説明: Explanations shown when you click a word in the code (English). tools/make_glossaries.py makes this file from the dictionaries in tools/glossary/en/ (fix the dictionaries, not this file).
$ ros2: The ROS 2 command. Used with run, launch, topic, node and so on after ros2
$ ros2 run: Runs one node (executable) in a package. ros2 run package executable
$ ros2 launch: Starts a set of nodes together with a launch file
$ ros2 node info: Shows a node's topics, services and actions
$ ros2 topic hz: How many messages arrive per second
$ ros2 topic info: A topic's type and the numbers of senders and receivers. -v also shows QoS
$ ros2 topic pub: Sends a message to a topic
$ ros2 --qos-reliability: Sets the QoS for receiving (best_effort or reliable)
$ ros2 service call: Calls a service. ros2 service call name type "{contents}"
$ ros2 action send_goal: Sends a goal to an action
$ ros2 interface: Inspects message, service and action types
$ ros2 interface show: Shows what a type contains (fields and their types)
$ ros2 pkg prefix: Shows where a package is installed
$ ros2 --build-type: The kind of package. ament_python (Python) or ament_cmake (C++, messages)
$ ros2 --dependencies: Writes the packages it uses (depends on) into package.xml from the start
$ ros2 --ros-args: Everything after this is ROS settings (-p for parameters, -r for renaming)
$ ros2 bag info: What a recording contains, and how many of each
$ ros2 doctor: Checks the ROS 2 environment for problems
$ ros2 --frame-id: The name of the parent coordinate frame
$ ros2 --child-frame-id: The name of the child coordinate frame
$ ros2 serial -b: Serial speed (bps). Match the flight controller's SERIALn_BAUD
$ ros2 serial -D: The serial device (/dev/ttyAMA0 and so on)
$ ros2 udp4 -p: The UDP port the Agent listens on (match ArduPilot's DDS_UDP_PORT)
$ rviz2: A tool that shows a robot's position, sensors and coordinate frames in 3D
$ rqt_graph: A tool that shows how nodes and topics connect as a diagram
$ colcon: The tool that builds a ROS 2 workspace
$ colcon build: Builds the packages in the workspace. Always run it at the top of the workspace
$ colcon --symlink-install: Links Python files instead of copying them, so changes need no rebuild
$ colcon --packages-up-to: Builds the given package and the packages it uses
$ rosdep: A tool that installs the libraries packages use, with apt and so on, all at once
$ rosdep install: Installs what the workspace's packages use
$ rosdep --ignore-src: Does not install things whose source is in the workspace
$ rosdep --rosdistro: The ROS 2 version (jazzy and so on)
$ vcs: A tool that fetches many repositories at once (vcstool)
$ vcs import: Fetches all the repositories listed in a .repos file
$ vcs --input: The .repos file to read (a URL is fine)
$ install/setup.bash: The settings file that makes your own workspace's packages usable
$ /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash: The settings file that makes ROS 2 Jazzy usable
$ ~/.bashrc: The settings file loaded every time you open a terminal
$ sim_vehicle.py: Starts ArduPilot's SITL (simulation inside the computer)
$ sim_vehicle.py -v: The kind of vehicle (ArduCopter, Rover, ArduPlane and so on)
$ sim_vehicle.py -I: The vehicle's instance number (when running several)
$ mavproxy.py --aircraft: The name of the folder to save logs in
$ Tools/environment_install/install-prer: A script that installs what ArduPilot's build and SITL need
$ ./gradlew assemble: Builds and packages it into a runnable form
rclpy.node: The module containing Node (the node class)
Node: A ROS 2 node. In rclpy, inherit from it to make your own node. In launch, it describes a node to start
spin: Keeps running timer and receive handlers until Ctrl + C
spin_once: Runs the receive and timer handlers just once
spin_until_future_complete: Runs the handlers and waits until a future (such as a service answer) arrives
try_shutdown: Shuts ROS 2 down (no error if it is already shut down)
get_logger: Gets the tool for writing logs (the logger)
log: A variable holding the logger. Print with log.info()
create_publisher: Makes a sender (publisher). (type, topic name, QoS)
create_subscription: Makes a receiver (subscriber). (type, topic name, callback, QoS)
create_timer: Makes a timer that calls a function at fixed intervals. (seconds, function)
create_service: Makes the answering side of a service (server). (type, name, callback)
create_client: Makes the asking side of a service (client). (type, name)
wait_for_service: Waits until the service is available. timeout_sec is how many seconds to wait
call_async: Calls a service (the answer goes into a future later)
future: A container for an answer that arrives later. Take it out with result()
result: Takes out the answer (future.result()). In ArmMotors' answer, whether arming succeeded
declare_parameter: Declares a parameter (name and default value)
get_parameter: Gets a parameter. .value is its value
get_clock: The node's clock (can follow simulation time too)
to_msg: Converts to message form (such as a Header's stamp)
qos_profile_sensor_data: The QoS for sensors (BEST_EFFORT). Used when receiving ArduPilot's topics
Request: What a service request contains (example: ModeSwitch.Request(mode=4))
std_msgs: Basic message types (String, Float64, Header and so on)
String: A string message. Its content is data
data: The message's content (for String, the string)
geometry_msgs: Message types for position, orientation and velocity
PoseStamped: Position and orientation (with time and coordinate frame)
header: The message's header (stamp is the time, frame_id the coordinate frame's name)
Header: The message header type (time and coordinate frame name)
frame_id: The coordinate frame's name. For /ap/cmd_vel, "map" (east, north, up) or "base_link" (the vehicle's heading)
example_interfaces: Practice message and service types included in ROS 2
AddTwoInts: A service type that adds two integers (a, b → sum)
ardupilot_msgs: Message and service types for ArduPilot's DDS
ModeSwitch: The mode change service type (mode → status, curr_mode)
Request.alt: The height to take off to (m)
launch: The library of launch file parts
launch_ros: Launch parts for ROS 2 (Node and so on)
LaunchDescription: The list of things to start (nodes and so on)
generate_launch_description: The entry function of a launch file. Returns a LaunchDescription
Node.output: Where logs go ("screen" for the screen)
entry_points: Registers command names and the functions they call (console_scripts)
console_scripts: name usable with ros2 run = module:function
data_files: Files installed together (launch files and so on)
rosidl_default_generators: Tools that generate code from message types
rosidl_generate_interfaces: Generates Python and C++ code from .msg and .srv files
rosidl_default_runtime: What is needed at run time to use the generated message types
rosidl_interface_packages: A marker saying this is a message type package
ament_package: Packages it as a ROS 2 package (written at the end of CMakeLists.txt)
depend: A package used (needed for both building and running)
buildtool_depend: A package used as a build tool
exec_depend: A package used only when running
member_of_group: The package's group (rosidl_interface_packages for message types)
REQUIRED: Makes it an error if not found (CMake)
DEPENDENCIES: The packages of other types this message type uses
pymavlink: A library for using MAVLink from Python
mavutil: pymavlink's handy functions for connecting and so on
mavlink: Definitions (constants) of MAVLink messages and commands
wait_heartbeat: Waits until a HEARTBEAT ("I'm alive" signal) arrives. Tells you the other side's system and component
target_system: The system ID of the other side (the vehicle)
target_component: The ID of the other side's part (component)
mode_mapping: A dictionary from mode names to numbers
mav: The collection of functions that send MAVLink messages (..._send)
recv_match: Waits for and receives a message of the given kind
recv_match.type: The kind of message to wait for ("COMMAND_ACK" and so on)
recv_match.timeout: The maximum number of seconds to wait
COMMAND_ACK: The answer to a command (whether it was accepted)
GLOBAL_POSITION_INT: A message with latitude and longitude (×10⁷) and height (mm)
MAV_MODE_FLAG_CUSTOM_MODE_ENABLED: A flag meaning "use ArduPilot's own mode numbers"
MAV_CMD_SET_MESSAGE_INTERVAL: Asks for a given message to be sent at a given interval (microseconds)
MAV_CMD_NAV_TAKEOFF: The takeoff command. The 7th argument is the height (m)
set_position_target_local_ned_send: In GUIDED, gives a position or velocity in NED (north, east, down)
MAV_FRAME_LOCAL_NED: North, east, down coordinates with home as the origin
command: Which command the answer (COMMAND_ACK) is for
Unit: The section for the service's description and start order (systemd)
After: Start after this (network-online.target means after the network)
Service: The section for how to run the service
Restart: Whether to restart when it stops (always means always)
Install: The section for where to hook it in when enabled
WantedBy: multi-user.target makes it start automatically on a normal boot
ROS_DOMAIN_ID: The ROS 2 group number. Only nodes with the same number connect
DDS_DOMAIN_ID: ArduPilot's DDS group number. Match ROS_DOMAIN_ID
DDS_UDP_PORT: The port number when using DDS over UDP (default 2019)
SERIAL2_PROTOCOL: What SERIAL2 (TELEM2) is used for. 45 is DDS
SERIAL2_BAUD: SERIAL2's speed (921 is 921,600 bps, 115 is 115,200 bps)
SERIAL8_PROTOCOL: What SERIAL8 (on H7 FCs, often the second USB port) is used for. 45 is DDS
GUID_TIMEOUT: Seconds until stopping in GUIDED after velocity commands stop arriving (default 3)
FENCE_RADIUS: The geofence's maximum distance from home (m)
ARMING_CHECK: Checks before arming. Never set it to 0 (no checks) on a real vehicle
BATT_LOW_VOLT: The voltage at which the battery counts as low
cmd_gps_pose: The topic that gives a destination by latitude and longitude
prearm_check: The service that checks whether it is ready to arm (/ap/prearm_check)
takeoff: Takeoff. MAVProxy's takeoff 10 climbs to 10 m
throttle: arm throttle arms using the throttle channel (MAVProxy)
guided: GUIDED mode (moves by instructions from outside)
micro_ros_agent: The program that relays between XRCE-DDS (ArduPilot) and ordinary ROS 2
actions: Things launch starts (Node and so on)
status: Whether the service succeeded (the answer of ModeSwitch and Takeoff)
GUIDED: The mode that moves by instructions from outside (number 4 in Copter)
LAND: The mode that lands in place (number 9 in Copter)
$ ~/ros2_ws/install/setup.bash: The settings file that makes the packages in your workspace (~/ros2_ws) usable
$ ~/ardu_ws/install/setup.bash: The settings file that makes the packages in the ArduPilot workspace (~/ardu_ws) usable
$ docker: The Docker command. Handles containers and images
$ docker run: Makes a container from an image and runs it
$ docker --rm: Deletes the container automatically when it stops
$ docker -v: Connects a folder or volume into the container (-v outside:inside)
$ docker -it: Lets you operate it from the keyboard (-i takes input, -t uses a terminal)
$ docker -t: In docker build, the image's name (tag); in docker run, use a terminal
$ docker -w: The working folder inside the container
$ docker build: Makes an image from a Dockerfile
$ docker -f: Forces it (stops and deletes even if running, and so on)
$ docker exec: Runs a command inside a running container
$ docker system: Handles Docker as a whole (df shows space used, prune cleans up)
build: In compose.yaml, where the Dockerfile is (builds the image)
image: In compose.yaml, the image to use
run.host: "0.0.0.0" makes it reachable from outside the container too
import: Loads a module (another file or library). You can give it a short name with as, as in import numpy as np
from: Loads only part of a module. from datetime import date
def: Makes a function. After def name(arguments):, write the body indented
return: Returns the function's answer and ends the function
class: Makes a class (a blueprint bundling data and functions)
self: Inside a method, refers to "this object itself". Written as the method's first argument
__init__: The method called first when an object is made (the constructor). Sets the initial values
__name__: The current file's name. It is '__main__' only when the file is run directly
super: Calls the parent class. super().__init__() runs the parent's initialization
if: Runs only when the condition is true
for: Takes the contents of a container one at a time and repeats
while: Repeats while the condition is true
in: In for, "one at a time from..."; in a condition, "whether it is in..."
or: True when at least one is true
is: Whether two things are the same object. Used to check for None, as in x is None
pass: Does nothing (put where the grammar needs something)
try: Wraps code where an error may occur
except: What to do when an error occurs inside try. You can specify the kind, as in except ValueError:
finally: Always runs at the end, whether or not an error occurred
print.end: The text added at the end (default: a newline)
input: Reads one line from the keyboard (returned as a string)
len: The length (number of elements or characters)
range: Makes a run of integers. range(5) is 0–4, range(1, 6) is 1–5
list: Makes a list (an ordered, changeable container)
set: Makes a set (a container with no duplicates)
int: An integer. int("3") turns a string into an integer
type: Checks the type of a value
keys: The list of a dictionary's keys
get: Gets a value from a dictionary. If the key is missing, returns None (or the second argument)
join: Joins the strings in a list with text in between. ", ".join(names)
os: A module for handling the OS (files, folders, environment variables)
os.path: Handles file paths (location strings). os.path.join joins them correctly
sys: A module for information about Python itself
argv: The list of arguments when run as a command. sys.argv[1] is the first
sleep: Waits for the given number of seconds
monotonic: Seconds on a clock that never goes backwards. Used to measure elapsed time
dump: Writes to a file as JSON
load: Reads a JSON file into dictionaries and lists
glob: Returns a list of files matching a file name pattern (*.py and so on)
KeyboardInterrupt: The exception raised when you stop with Ctrl + C
venv: A Python virtual environment (a per-project place for libraries)
pip: The tool for installing Python libraries
$ sudo:
Origin: short for superuser do (run as the administrator).
Runs the following command with administrator rights. Needed to change system settings or install software.
It asks for your password the first time (nothing appears on screen as you type).
$ apt:
Origin: short for Advanced Package Tool.
The command that manages software on Ubuntu. It installs and removes software.
$ apt install:
Installs software from the internet.
Example: sudo apt install pipx installs pipx.
$ cd:
Origin: short for change directory.
Moves to another folder in the terminal.
$ ssh:
Origin: short for Secure Shell.
Logs in to a computer across the network. git also uses it to talk to GitHub.
$ git: Software that records changes to source code. It keeps track of when and what changed, lets you go back to an earlier state, and lets you put code on GitHub.
$ git clone: Downloads a whole repository (a complete set of source code) from the internet.
$ git add: Picks the changes to go into the next commit.
. means "the current folder".
Puts every change in the current folder into the next commit (except what is listed in .gitignore).
$ git status: Shows the list of changed files, staged files and new files, and whether you are ahead of GitHub. When in doubt, start with this.
$ git log:
Origin: a log is a record or diary.
Shows the commit history, newest first. Quit with q.
$ git log -p:
Origin: -p is short for patch (the difference made by a change).
Also shows what each commit changed. Add a file name to see only that file.
$ git show: With a commit number, shows that commit's description and what it changed.
$ git master: The name of the main branch used in older repositories. Today, main is normal.
$ git -m:
Origin: -m is short for message.
Write the commit description inside quotes (").
$ &&:
If the previous command succeeded, runs the next one.
git add . && git commit -m "…" is the same as typing the two in order.
$ apt update: Refreshes the list of software (which versions are available). Do it before apt install
Loads a settings file into the current terminal (the same as source)
$ grep:
Origin: short for global regular expression print.
Picks out only the lines that contain some text.
Example: | grep 2e8a keeps only the lines containing 2e8a.
$ |:
Origin: a pipe, like data flowing through a pipe.
Passes the result of the command on the left to the command on the right.
$ python3:
Origin: version 3 of Python.
Runs a Python program on the PC.
$ /dev/ttyACM0:
The Pico's serial port. Linux treats devices like files too.
A second one gets a higher number, such as ttyACM1.
$ echo:
Origin: an echo.
Outputs the text you write as it is.
$ mkdir:
Origin: short for make directory.
Makes a folder.
$ mkdir -p:
Origin: -p is short for parents.
Also makes the folders along the way. No error if it already exists.
$ systemctl:
Origin: short for system control.
The command that manages Linux services. The Pico does not have it.
$ systemctl enable: Sets a service to start automatically at boot.
$ systemctl --now: In addition to the setting, starts it running right now.
$ journalctl:
Origin: short for journal control. A journal is a record.
Shows Linux logs.
$ journalctl -u:
Origin: -u is short for unit.
Shows only the logs of the given service.
$ pip:
Origin: said to be short for pip installs packages.
Installs Python libraries. It cannot be used on the Pico.
$ apt upgrade: Updates the installed software to newer versions.
$ git clone --branch: Specifies the version (branch or tag) to download.
$ git submodule: Works with other repositories used inside a repository (submodules).
$ git submodule update: Downloads the submodules. With --init, it also does the preparation needed the first time.
$ git --init: Also does the preparation needed the first time. git submodule update --init prepares and downloads the submodules in one go.
$ export: Sets an environment variable. export PICO_SDK_PATH=... tells the build where the SDK is.
$ source: Loads settings written in a file into the current terminal. source ~/.bashrc makes settings you just added usable right away.
$ python3 -m: Runs a Python module as a command. python3 -m serial.tools.miniterm runs pyserial's serial monitor.
$ python3 -c: Runs the following string as Python code
$ journalctl -f: Keeps showing new log lines as they come
$ git --branch: Chooses the branch (or tag) to fetch
$ apt -y: Answers "yes" automatically (does not ask for confirmation)
$ apt install -y: Answers "yes" automatically (does not ask for confirmation)
$ bash: Starts the shell (bash). -c runs the following string as a command
$ curl: Downloads data from a URL (also used to call web APIs)
$ curl -o: Sets the file name to save to
$ wget: Downloads a file from a URL
$ grep -F: Searches for the text as it is, without regular expressions
$ awk: Splits lines and takes out chosen columns
$ dpkg: Handles Debian and Ubuntu packages (.deb) directly
$ locale: Shows the current language and character encoding settings
$ locale-gen: Makes language and character encoding settings (locales)
$ add-apt-repository: Adds a place (repository) where apt looks for software
$ add-apt-repository universe: Enables the software store managed by the Ubuntu community
$ usermod -aG: Adds the user to a group (-a adds, -G is group). Takes effect after logging in again
$ venv: The module that makes Python virtual environments
$ systemctl daemon-reload: Makes systemd reread service files after you change them
$ git --recurse-submodules: Also fetches submodules (other repositories used inside)
$ git checkout: Switches to a branch or tag
